extraction.name: FOMO60K
extraction.description: A large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain MRI scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources, including both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and anatomical and pathological variability.
extraction.creator: Asbjørn Munk; Stefano Cerri; Jakob Ambsdorf; Julia Machnio; Sebastian Nørgaard Llambias; Vardan Nersesjan; Christian Hedeager Krag; Peirong Liu; Pablo Rocamora García; Mostafa Mehdipour Ghazi; Mikael Boesen; Michael Eriksen Benros; Juan Eugenio Iglesias; Mads Nielsen
extraction.citeAs: To ensure proper attribution and recognition of the source datasets we kindly ask all users to cite the following papers: OASIS1, OASIS2, BraTS24, MSD Braintumor, IXI, MGH Wild, NKI.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was aggregated from 16 publicly available datasets of brain MRI scans.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some scans lacked reliable sequence metadata.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Brain MRI scans from 16 publicly available source datasets, stored in NIfTI-compressed format.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MRI preprocessing comprised reorienting images to RAS orientation, affine co-registration, DWI-specific extraction and averaging steps, and skull-stripping when needed for anonymization.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Sequence metadata is unavailable for some scans, and skull-stripping was applied only when images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the provider or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for self-supervised pretraining, fine-tuning, development, and benchmarking of self-supervised learning methods in medical imaging.

description.evidence: We present FOMO60K, a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. The dataset includes both clinical- and research-grade images, multiple MRI sequences, and a wide range of anatomical and pathological variability, including scans with large brain anomalies.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We present FOMO60K, a large-scale, heterogeneous dataset of 60,529 brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans from 13,900 sessions and 11,187 subjects, aggregated from 16 publicly available sources. All MRI scans are stored in NIfTI-compressed format and organized using a standardized directory structure.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: MRI preprocessing comprised three main steps: reorienting images to RAS (Right–Anterior–Superior) orientation, affine co-registration, and skull-stripping. All scans were first reoriented to RAS and affinely co-registered using the mri_coreg command from FreeSurfer 7.4.130, with default parameters. For diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) scans stored in 4D format, additional steps were applied. If a b=0 (non-diffusionweighted) volume was available, it was extracted and saved separately. For the b=1000 shell, three diffusion-weighted volumes were selected based on their gradient directions being most closely aligned with the canonical x, y, and z axes. The corresponding volumes were averaged to produce a single representative 3D image. Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg31(FreeSurfer 7.4.1), which outputs segmentation masks of brain structures.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Skull-stripping was performed using SynthSeg31(FreeSurfer 7.4.1), which outputs segmentation masks of brain structures.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: The dataset will continue to grow in future releases as additional cohorts and modalities become available.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: "Unknown" indicates that scan sequence metadata was not available or could not be reliably identified. Skull-stripping was only applied when the images were not already defaced or skull-stripped by the dataset provider, or when visual inspection identified residual cranial features that could compromise anonymization.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: FOMO60K is intended to support the development and benchmarking of self-supervised leaming methods in medical imaging at scale. We also release code for self-supervised pretraining and fine-tuning to facilitate benchmarking, method development, and broader adoption of SSL in medical imaging. The dataset can be used with no further pre-processing for pre-training.
